contexts.text: Heaven and the Church are united to the Lord through proprium... for without proprium (or what is their Own) there is no union.
For all gathering together and union are from charity; and all dispersion and disunion are from no charity.
This one is that mystical union of which some think; which union is solely through love.
This union, which makes the image and likeness, cannot be so clearly seen in the human race; but it can in Heaven...
In the Lord alone was there... a union of the corporeal things with the Divine celestial things; and of the sensuous things with the Divine spiritual things.
For each and all things exist and subsist from... the unition of His Human essence, in as it were a marriage, with His Divine essence...

With no man have the internal man and the external ever been united; nor could they be united; nor can they be united; but in the Lord alone... With regenerated men it appears as if they had been united. Explained. AC 1577:4.

In the Lord alone has the internal man been united to the external; but in no other man, except in so far as the Lord has united, and does unite them. Love and charity, that is, good, is what alone unites; and (this) is solely from the Lord. Such is the union signified by these words. Explained.
The Lord came into the world that He might conjoin and unite the external man to the internal, that is, the Human essence to the Divine essence.
A man a brother = union.
Conjunction or union has been effected with the Celestial of love...
The unition was effected successively... Every temptation and victory united; and in proportion as He united Himself to Jehovah... intellectual truth was united to Divine good.
It treats (in ) of the union of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence; and of the Human essence with the Divine... AC 1986.
By these things Abraham represented the union of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence; and in fact that of His internal man, which was Jehovah, with His Rational. AC 1996.
The Lord united the affection of truth to the affection of good... when He united the Human essence to the Divine essence.
By this Internal (of man) the Lord is united to man.
His Human essence, by the unition, was in like manner made life.
The union of the Divine essence with the Human essence. Signified, Explained.
The union of the Human essence with the Divine essence. Signified, Explained.
The Angels perceive... the reciprocal union of His Divine essence with His Human... and of His Human with His Divine.
That the unition was effected reciprocally. Explained.
As to the union of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence, and of His Human essence with His Divine essence, it infinitely transcends [the human understanding]. Explained.
There was a union of the Lord with Jehovah; but there is no union of man with the Lord; but conjunction.
The Lord, by His Own power, united Himself to Jehovah...

It is this reciprocal union which is meant in ; in which words are hidden most arcane things about the union of good with truth, and of truth with good; or, what is the same, of the union of the Divine essence with the Human essence, and of the Human essence with the Divine essence...

In , are the same arcana concerning the union of good with truth, and of truth with good, or, what is the same, of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence... This is that mystical union of which many speak.

The union of the Lord's Human essence with His Divine essence is circumstanced as is that of truth with good; and the union of His Divine essence with His Human essence, as that of good with truth, which is a reciprocal union. Nay, in the Lord, it was truth itself which united itself to good; and good which united itself to truth...
A covenant = union. AC 2084.
But there is union when the countenance, speech, and gesture are in agreement with the thought.

The covenant first mentioned refers to the union of Jehovah with the Human essence; and the second, to the conjunction with those who are the seed. In order that a more distinct idea may be had (of these two things) we may call the former a union, and the latter a conjunction. There was a union of the Divine essence with the Human essence; but there is a conjunction of the Lord with the human race; for the Lord is life, and His Human essence also was made life; and there is a union of life with, life; whereas man is (only) a recipient of life...
A union still closer. Signified, Explained.

The unition of the Human essence with the Divine essence was not effected all at once; but through the whole course of His life... Thus He continually ascended to glorification, that is, union. Signified. AC 2063:2.
That in His union with the Father, the Lord had in view His conjunction with the human race. Illustrated. AC 2077. AC 2102:2.
Glorification = union.
That the Rational of His Human essence should then be united to the Divine essence. Signified, Explained. AC 2095.
The state of union then, Signified, Explained.
The state of the Lord's perception... before the perfect union... Treated of. AC 2136.
His perceptions were more and more interior, in proportion as He drew near to union with Jehovah.
By Abraham's hundredth year, is signified the full unition of the Human of the Lord with the Divine, and of the Divine with the Human. AC 2636.

The Lord's love towards the universal human race was so great that He willed to save all to eternity through the unition of the Human essence with the Divine essence, and of the Divine essence with the Human essence. AC 2235:6.
For all things said in the Word involve the advent of the Lord, to unite the Human essence to the Divine essence; through which unition He should save the human race.
Then the Lord came into the world, and through the unition of the Divine essence with the Human essence in Himself, He conjoined Heaven with earth...
The Angels are enlightened and confirmed by these things more and more in regard to the unition of the Lord's Human essence with His Divine essence.
But when the Human essence had become united to the Divine essence... He no longer interceded, but He has mercy, and... saves.
This life (of love towards the universal human race) is the veriest Celestial through which He united Himself to the Divine, and the Divine to Himself.
They represented (before the little children) the unition of the Lord's Human with the Divine.
Thus the Word is the uniting medium of Heaven and earth; the union is through the Church; in fact through the Word in the Church.
Salvation through the unition of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence. Signified.
The good were separated from the evil, and the former were saved and the latter condemned, solely through the unition of the Lord's Divine essence with His Human essence. Treated of.
These Divine perceptions and thoughts from Himself, He implanted in Divine intelligence and wisdom; and this even to the perfect union of His Human with His Divine.
The Lord's life itself was a continual progression of the Human to the Divine, oven to absolute union.
As to the state of the unition of the Divine Spiritual of the Lord in His Divine Celestial, it is the very marriage of good and truth... AC 2649.
The Divine Rational existed from the unition of the Divine Spiritual with the Divine Celestial.
Abraham made a great feast = dwelling together and union... As it treats of the union (of the Divine and the Human) it is called a great feast.

From the first verse of () it has treated of the unition of the Divine essence with the Human essence of the Lord, in this order: Of the presence of the Divine in the Human for the sake of unition, . Of the presence of the Human in the Divine, thus of reciprocal unition, . That by this unition the Human was made Divine, . And this successively and continuously while the Lord lived in the world, . That this commenced when the Rational was in a state to receive, . The state of the unition is described as to its quality, with its arcana, , and . AC 2667.

From the union of good and truth which inflows from the Lord, Heaven is compared to a marriage; (and) when good united to truth flows down into a lower sphere, it presents this union of minds; and, when into a still lower one, a marriage; and therefore the union of minds from good united to truth from the Lord, is conjugial love itself. AC 2734.
In () it treats of the Lord's most grievous and inmost temptations, through which He united the Human essence to the Divine essence. AC 2765. AC 2776.

The passion of the cross was the last of the Lord's temptation, through which He plenarily united the Human to the Divine, and the Divine to the Human, and thus glorified Himself. It is this very union through which those who have the faith of charity in Him can be saved. For the Supreme Divine itself could no longer reach the human race... and therefore in order that it might be able to descend to such men, the Lord came into the world, and united, in Himself, the Human to the Divine; which union could not be effected otherwise than through the most grievous combats and victories in temptations; and finally through the last one, which was that of the cross.

The illumination of the sight and understanding of the spiritual would not take place, unless the Lord had united the Human essence to the Divine essence; and, unless He had united them, man in the world would no longer have had any capacity for understanding and perceiving good and truth; nor would any spiritual Angel in Heaven...
The unition of the Divine essence and the Human essence was effected mutually and reciprocally. References.
For the union of the Divine essence with the Human essence, and of the Human essence with the Divine essence, is the Divine marriage of good with truth, and of truth with good...
That the Divine love is that through which the Lord united the Human essence to the Divine essence, and the Divine essence to the Human essence; or, what is the same, glorified Himself. References.
The unition of the Human with the Divine through the last of temptation. Signified, Explained. AC 2854.
That there was always a further unition of the Lord's Human essence with His Divine essence, even to a plenary unition. References.
The union of the Lord's Human essence with His Divine essence. Signified, Explained. (Through temptations. AC 3381, Signified, Explained.)
The full unition was accomplished after the last temptation...
That the Lord united His Divine essence to the Human essence through temptations by His Own power. References.
As through temptations, so also through these continual revelations from Himself, He united the Divine essence to the Human essence. Signified, Explained.
Whether (the Natural) could be united (to the Rational). Signified, Explained.
To kiss = unition and conjunction from affection. AC 3574.
Presence and unition. Signified, Explained.
Even to perfect union. Signified, Explained.
By His going again to the Father, is meant that He has united the Human essence to the Divine essence. Illustrated.

The supreme internal sense treats of the unition of the Human of the Lord with His Divine... and that He would be Jehovah as to the Divine Natural also through the unition of the Divine essence with the Human essence, and of the Human essence with the Divine essence. This unition is not to be understood as that of two who are distinct from each other, and who are only conjoined by love... but it is a real unition into a one...
This union is not a dwelling together...
Evils and goods... are not conjoined, still less united...
Finally, there succeeds (in marriage) a unition as to celestial good and spiritual truth. Explained.
A union of goods and truths. Signified, Explained.
Lest thus (truth natural and not spiritual) should be united. Signified, Explained.
Love is spiritual conjunction or unition.
Therefore, where there is not conjunction, or union, there is not being. Explained.
In the supreme sense, this treats of the Lord, how He has united the Internal with the External in His Human.
In the supreme sense, the Sabbath represented the union of the Divine and of the Divine Human in the Lord. AC 8886.
They came into the tent = what is holy of union... for love is union.

It treats in this verse of the union of Divine good with truth Divine; and as all union is first effected through the influx of the one into the other and the consequent perception; then through application; next through immission; and afterwards through conjunction, (these things are treated of in order).
Jethro represented Divine good united to Divine truth; hence by hearing his voice is signified consent from union. Explained.
The union of the Divine good in Heaven with the Divine truth there. Signified, Explained.
To call to Himself, when said of the Divine, = conjunction; here, union, because it is said of the Divine good united with the Divine truth, which, through conjunction, become a one.
That through the Word there is a union of Heaven and the world; thus of the Lord with the human race. References.
The preservation, through a complete unition, of good and truth... Signified, Explained.
In the supreme sense... the burnt-offerings = the unition of the Divine truth with the Divine good; which unition is what is meant by glorification...
Unition with the Divine good of the Divine love. Signified, Explained.

A Sabbath of a Sabbath = ... the union of the Human of the Lord with the Divine itself... For when the Lord... went out of the world, He made His Human the Divine good, through union with the Divine itself which was in Him.
For when the Lord had united His Human with the Divine itself, He had peace...
For the universal of all things is, that the Lord has united His Human to the Divine itself; and that from that there are peace and salvation for man.

The essential of marriage is a unition of minds; (therefore) such as are the minds, such is the unition; (and as) the mind is formed solely from truths and goods... it follows that the unition of minds is exactly such as are the truths and goods from which they have been formed; consequently, that a unition of minds which have been formed of genuine truths and goods is the most perfect one.
That the Lord has united the Divine truth to the Divine good; thus His Human to the Divine itself. (References to passages.)
That the full unition of the Divine and Human in Him has been effected through the passion of the cross. Explained.

The Lord said these things because the unition was reciprocal, of the Divine with the Human, and of the Human with the Divine... It is the like with all unition, which, unless it is reciprocal, is not full...
Therefore an Angel is an Angel of Heaven Recording to the union of love and wisdom in him. It is the like with a man of the Church...
Those who believe themselves wise from confirmations in favour of the mystical union of the Divine and the Human in the Lord. Signified, Explained.
By the mystical union, which is also called the hypostatical union, are meant their figments about the influx and operation of the Divinity into the Lord's Humanity as into another...
For such was the union of their minds, from which their speech flows. Described.
For no married partners can be received into Heaven, so as to remain there, except those who have been interiorly united, or who can be united, as into a one. Explained.
That the inclination to unite herself to the man is constant and perpetual with a wife; but is inconstant and alternate with the man. Explained.
Hence there takes place in an effective manner a union of souls, and a conjunction of minds. Explained.
That those who are in love truly conjugial feel themselves a united man... Explained.
It follows that the unition of soul and mind with a married partner is felt in the body also as one flesh.
That, regarded in itself, love truly conjugial is a union of souls, and a conjunction of minds... Explained.
That conjugial pairs are born... he confirmed... also by the inmost and eternal union of minds...

Those who have lived in love truly conjugial... do not want a repeated marriage... because 1. they have been united as to their souls, and thence as to their minds; and this union, being spiritual, is an actual adjunction of the soul and mind of the one to those of the other, which cannot possibly be dissolved... 2. Because they have also been united as to their bodies through the reception of the propagations of the soul of the husband by the wife; and thus by the insertion of his life into hers... and, reciprocally, through the reception by the husband of the conjugial love of the wife...
That by the same acts the Lord united Himself to the Father; and the Father [united]. Himself to Him. General article.
That the Father and the Son, that is, the Divine and the Human, in the Lord, have been united like the soul and the body... TCR 98, Explained.
That the union is reciprocal. Illustrated.
The reason the union is reciprocal, is that no union or conjunction between two is possible, unless the one reciprocally accedes to the other. Explained, examples.
That the progression to union was the state of His exinanition; and that the union itself is the state of His glorification. General article.
The glorification is the unition of the Human of the Lord with the Divine of His Father: this unition was effected successively; and fully through the passion of the cross. Explained.

A discourse about union: that nothing is possible of which any faculty or quality can be predicated unless there are a number... and also that no union is possible... unless everyone loves the neighbour more than himself...
a. On those who have consulted together about a union of religions...
Thus united the Divine Human to the Divine itself... AE 659:19.
To the conjunction and union accomplished in time.

For the Divine good and Divine truth proceed from the Lord united; and therefore they must be united in an Angel of Heaven and a man of the Church. This union is never possible except through the marriage of two minds into a one. Explained.
Such is the union, through love, of the Lord with man, and of man with the Lord.
3. The union of love and wisdom is reciprocal: love unites itself to wisdom, and wisdom unites itself back to love...
Redeemer. 8. That after the union was accomplished, He returned into the Divine in which He had been from eternity, together with and in the glorified Human. Chapter.
